assumptions: For each reduction-tree level h, ell h is the b-by-b unit-lower GEPP factor used in the proof of Theorem 3.6.
Every strict-lower entry of ell h has absolute value at most one, as stated in the proof.
probeIn h represents the paper's bounded vector Abar_h * Ubar_(h+1)^(-1), and probeOut h is its exact inverse action, recorded by ell h * probeOut h = probeIn h.
z (h+1) is obtained by applying the next inverse factor to z h, recorded by the full entrywise level equation.
Both the one-level probe inputs and the initial repeated-product vector are bounded componentwise by one.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p43_t3_calu_multiplier_growth (b H : Nat) (ell : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Real) (probeIn probeOut z : Nat -> Nat -> Real) (hp : P43CALUMultiplierProcess b H ell probeIn probeOut z) : (forall h<H, forall i<b, abs (probeOut h i) <= 2^i) and (forall i<b, abs (z H i) <= 2^(b*H))
formal_statement.plain_language: Each bounded inverse action in the proof of Theorem 3.6 satisfies its rowwise power-of-two estimate, and after H reduction-tree levels every CALU multiplier is bounded by 2^(bH).

informal_proof: Split each unit-lower matrix equation at its diagonal. Entries above the diagonal vanish and the diagonal entry is one, so forward substitution gives the current component as the right-hand side minus a sum over earlier components. Strong induction and the geometric sum 1+sum_{k<i}2^k=2^i give the bounded inverse-action estimate. Apply the same bound at each of the H levels and combine powers to obtain 2^(bH).
informal_statement: Prove the one-level unit-lower inverse-action estimate explicitly stated in the proof of Theorem 3.6 and the theorem's final CALU multiplier bound 2^(bH).
